narr: Torrential training rainfall redeveloped overnight heading into the 17th, this time over portions of Western Kentucky in the Pennyrile region. Rainfall totals reached 2-7 inches with flooding observed in Livermore, Providence, Madisonville, and several towns in Muhlenberg County. As was the case in the morning, the greater PW values near 2.2 inches had shifted to Western Kentucky, with 850mb moisture transport focused on the area. A slow moving boundary resided to the north, channeling moisture along the boundary on the south side.
ev: Water flowed over US-41 about 1.1 miles north of Providence. Overnight rainfall totals had radar estimated and measurements of 3 to 5 inches in portions of southern Webster County north of Providence.
The S 2nd St underpass under the West Kentucky Parkway flooded in Central City. A CWOP station in Central City reported 4.48in of rain from 2200-0130CST.

Significant street flooding occurred in Madisonville. Water encroached on I-69 near Exit 114. Radar estimated rainfall of 2.5-3.5 inches of rainfall occurred from 0000-0200CST. A rain gage 6 miles east of Madisonville measured 4.17 inches of rain as of 0135CST.
Most of KY-2110 flooded due to torrential rainfall. Overnight rainfall in Livermore measured 5.24in.
Water covered N Main St on the north side of Greenville. Overnight rainfall measured 3 inches at a Greenville CoCoRaHS gage while a Mesonet gage 3 miles NW of Powderly measured 4.14 inches.
Water was across KY-181 near the entrance to Cal-Maine Foods. Radar estimated 6-hr rainfall was 4-6 inches, with the rainiest hour amounting to around 2 inches from 2300-0000CST.
